body:
### What version of Codex CLI is running?

`codex-cli 0.156.1` (observed locally on 2026-09-29). The user reports being unable to upgrade to 0.159.1; that is a separate problem.

### What subscription do you have?

Signed in with a ChatGPT account. Exact subscription tier is not confirmed.

### Which model were you using?

`gpt-6.1-sol`

### What platform is your computer?

Windows x64, PowerShell.

### Codex doctor report

Not collected. The current CLI is already having resume/compaction problems, and I did not run additional interactive diagnostics.

### What issue are you seeing?

When the user tried to select GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex CLI with ChatGPT sign-in, the CLI returned HTTP 400 with the exact error below:

```json
{"type":"error","status":400,"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"The 'gpt-6.1-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}}
```

The CLI did not make clear whether the cause was rollout status, subscription eligibility, an older client, or an authentication/model-list mismatch.

### What steps can reproduce the bug?

1. Sign in to Codex CLI using a ChatGPT account on Windows.
2. Attempt to use `gpt-6.1-sol` in the CLI.
3. Observe the unsupported-with-ChatGPT-account response.

The exact selection method and account tier were not captured; the response body above was provided by the user. Please investigate the eligibility check and error path for this model on CLI 0.156.1.

### What is the expected behavior?

For an eligible account where rollout has reached the user, GPT-6.1 Sol should work in Codex CLI. Otherwise, the CLI should state the specific reason access is unavailable and what, if anything, the user can do. Current OpenAI model documentation lists GPT-6.1 Sol for Plus, Pro, Business, Enterprise, and Edu in the Codex CLI rollout, with Enterprise/Edu administrator enablement and plan/client/rollout qualifications: https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models

### Additional information

This is separate from an existing report about CLI resume/compaction hangs. No private session transcript, account identifier, or authentication material is included here.

comments.body: same here with codex-cli 0.156.2. And models list does not have gpt-6.1-sol.

I encountered the same HTTP 400 error for `gpt-6.1-sol` while signed in with a ChatGPT Pro $100 account. Signing out and back in did not resolve it.

Running this command fixed it for me:

```sh
codex app-server daemon update
```

After updating the app-server daemon, I could use `gpt-6.1-sol` again.

It seems there’s still a version mismatch between the codex clients on my Windows machine:
The CLI is updated to v0.159.2.
The background app-server daemon is still running v0.157.0, which predates gpt-6.1-sol. Unfortunately, for me, attempts to update the daemon fail with `host Job Object prevents daemon detachment`.
The VS Code extension still has an older codex release as well.

For now, `codex --no-daemon` works around the stale background server. I can select and use gpt-6.1-sol when I launch codex this way.

Additional Windows reproduction on codex-cli 0.159.2, with the subscription tier confirmed by the user as ChatGPT Pro ($200), personal workspace.

Environment:
- Windows, PowerShell
- Standalone Codex CLI: codex-cli 0.159.2 (verified locally)
- codex login status: Logged in using ChatGPT (verified locally)
- Requested model: gpt-6.1-sol
- Reasoning effort: low
- User reports that the same model works in the Windows ChatGPT desktop GUI, while the standalone CLI fails. These are distinct client paths; desktop success does not establish CLI entitlement.

Observed error:
```json
{"type":"error","status":400,"error":{"type":"invalid_request_error","message":"The 'gpt-6.1-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."}}
```

The existing local logs confirm the error on September 30, 2026 at 20:20:42 UTC (13:20:42 PDT). The CLI successfully connected to wss://chatgpt.com/backend-api/codex/responses; the request metadata recorded ChatGPT authentication, model gpt-6.1-sol, and reasoning effort low; then the turn received the error above. Startup WebSocket prewarm also received the same error.

A local model cache fetched on September 30, 2026 at 20:21:28 UTC identifies client version 0.159.2 and lists gpt-6.1-sol with visibility=list and default reasoning effort low. This cache is in a shared Codex home, so it does not independently prove live CLI eligibility or identify which client fetched it.

Official model guidance includes Pro and Codex CLI in the GPT-6.1 Sol rollout, subject to account/client availability:
https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/models
The model documentation supports low reasoning effort:
https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/models/gpt-6.1-sol

Expected behavior: If the account is eligible in the CLI, the request should work. If access differs between desktop and CLI, the rejection should explain the specific restriction or rollout status.

Please investigate the desktop-versus-CLI access discrepancy on Windows CLI 0.159.2. The available evidence does not establish whether the cause is rollout gating, client request compatibility, or backend routing/eligibility state. No workaround or configuration repair has been verified.

No authentication material, account identifiers, full transcripts, or raw log files are included.

update, an unrelated issue (https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/48074#issuecomment-5902036562) informed me to update the codex daemon.   doing that then fixed this `gpt-6.1-sol` issue for me.  Win x64.

```
// finish up your codex sessions, then run:
codex app-server daemon update --from-cli --yes
codex app-server daemon restart
codex app-server daemon version
```

you should then have `0.159.2` or above.

I was able to fix this on Linux (Codex CLI 0.159.3).

In my case, the CLI itself was already 0.159.3, but the running app-server was still an older version:

```text
managedCodexVersion: 0.159.3
cliVersion:          0.159.3
appServerVersion:    0.158.0
```

Before fixing it:
- codex debug models already contained gpt-6.1-sol
- /model did not show GPT-6.1 Sol
- forcing codex -m gpt-6.1-sol showed the model locally, but sending a prompt returned:
400 invalid_request_error:
"The 'gpt-6.1-sol' model is not supported when using Codex with a ChatGPT account."

I then tried:
```text
codex app-server daemon update --from-cli --yes
```

but initially got:
```text
Error: app server is running but is not managed by codex app-server daemon
```

I checked the running processes and found an old 0.158.0 app-server still running in the background, even though all Codex sessions had been closed:
```text
.../releases/0.158.0-.../bin/codex app-server --listen unix:// --managed-daemon
.../releases/0.158.0-.../bin/codex app-server daemon pid-update-loop
```

After terminating those stale processes, I ran:
```text
codex app-server daemon update --from-cli --yes
codex app-server daemon start
```

The first start timed out waiting for the control socket, but the new 0.159.3 app-server process was actually running. Shortly afterward:
```text
codex app-server daemon version
```

returned:
```text
managedCodexVersion: 0.159.3
cliVersion:          0.159.3
appServerVersion:    0.159.3
```

After that, GPT-6.1 Sol appeared normally in /model, and a real request using gpt-6.1-sol succeeded.
So in my case, the cause was a stale 0.158.0 app-server process remaining in the background after the CLI/managed package had already been updated to 0.159.3. Updating/restarting the daemon after removing that stale process fixed the issue.
